title: Countably generated flat Mittag-Leffler modules are projective
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $P$ an $R$-module. Assume $P$ is flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], Mittag-Leffler [def-trf-mittag-leffler-module], and countably generated: there is a countable subset $E\subseteq P$ such that every element of $P$ is a finite $R$-linear combination of elements of $E$. Then $P$ is projective over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-projective-module].

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-countable-flat-ml-sequential-presentation] to $R,P$ with the given flatness, tensor-product Mittag-Leffler condition and at most countable generating set. Obtain a sequence $G_n\cong R^{r_n}$, maps $u_n:G_n\to G_{n+1}$ and compatible maps $\iota_n:G_n\to P$ that exhibit $P$ as its colimit, indexed by the positive integers.

source.place: Tag 059X (lemma-countgen-projective), opening paragraph; sequential form following Tag 059W.

proof.text: Each $G_n$ is finitely presented, using $R^0\to R^{r_n}\to G_n\to0$ and $G_n\cong R^{r_n}$. The positive integers form a small nonempty directed poset. Apply [lem-trf-mittag-leffler-hom-systems] to this diagram and the actual colimit cocone $(P,(\iota_n))$ from step 1. For every $R$-module $N$ and $n\ge1$, obtain $c\ge n$ such that for all $k\ge c$ the images of $\operatorname{Hom}_R(G_k,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(G_n,N)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_R(G_c,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(G_n,N)$ agree. Their maps are precomposition with $u_{k-1}\cdots u_n$ and $u_{c-1}\cdots u_n$, with an empty composite the identity. These are exactly the composites of $h\mapsto h u_n$. Equal submodules have equal underlying subgroups, so this inverse sequence is ML by [def-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler-system], with stabilization index $c(n)=c$.

source.place: Tag 059X, Hom-system assertion, justified by Tags 059M (proposition-ML-tensor) and 059E (proposition-ML-characterization), condition (4).

proof.text: Fix any short exact sequence $0\to N_1\xrightarrow{a}N_2\xrightarrow{b}N_3\to0$. Apply [lem-trf-sequential-free-colimit-hom-exact] to the same finite-free stages, cocone and colimit $P$ from step 1. Step 2 with $N=N_1$ supplies its kernel-system ML hypothesis, so $0\to\operatorname{Hom}_R(P,N_1)\xrightarrow{a\circ-}\operatorname{Hom}_R(P,N_2)\xrightarrow{b\circ-}\operatorname{Hom}_R(P,N_3)\to0$ is exact. Thus $\operatorname{Hom}_R(P,-)$ is exact. Explicitly, for any surjection $b:X\to Y$, the inclusion $\ker b\hookrightarrow X$ is injective with image exactly $\ker b$, so $0\to\ker b\to X\xrightarrow{b}Y\to0$ meets the helper's hypotheses; use step 2 at $N=\ker b$. Surjectivity of the literal map $b\circ-$ supplies, for every $h:P\to Y$, a lift $\widetilde h:P\to X$ with $b\widetilde h=h$. Hence $P$ is projective by [def-weil-pbc-projective-module].
